definitions.explanation: A smaller earthquake that follows the main shock. Composed of 余 (remaining, leftover) + 震 (quake, tremor). In earthquake-prone Japan, aftershocks are frequently reported in the news and are an important part of daily earthquake awareness.

examples.japanese: {余震|よしん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
{本震|ほんしん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧、⟦{何度|なんど}→何度：17592_nando⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{余震|よしん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いた→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧。
examples.english: After the main quake, aftershocks continued many times.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大|おお}きな→大きな：02849_ookina⟧⟦{地震|じしん}→地震：01608_jishin⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{一週間|いっしゅうかん}→一週間：10979_isshuukan⟧⟦{経|た}って→経つ：09892_tatsu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦まだ→まだ：00603_mada⟧{余震|よしん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{感|かん}じられる→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧。
examples.english: Even a week after the major earthquake, aftershocks can still be felt.

notes:
USAGE:
After a major earthquake in Japan, news broadcasts will regularly report on {余震|よしん} activity. The phrase {余震|よしん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧ (be cautious of aftershocks) is a standard warning. The main earthquake is called {本震|ほんしん}, and foreshocks are called {前震|ぜんしん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {余震|よしん}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧ (be cautious of aftershocks)
- {余震|よしん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}く→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧ (aftershocks continue)
- {余震|よしん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{収|おさ}まる→収まる：11858_osamaru⟧ (aftershocks subside)
- ⟦{強|つよ}い→強い：00820_tsuyoi⟧{余震|よしん} (strong aftershock)
- {余震|よしん}⟦{活動|かつどう}→活動：00201_katsudou⟧ (aftershock activity)
